we have developed a novel framework for disseminating data in smart electric grids that is based on the applications data needs and semantics and that we have evaluated our approach using real data from a PMU network and have demonstrated that it results in lower processing overheads and bandwidth usage compared to the traditional approach.

(i) We propose a novel approach for disseminating data packets from PMUs in the Smart Grid, and (ii) we show that our approach results in a reduction in bandwidth requirements by 50% and in latency reduction by 30% for large PMU data size.
we propose and implement an approach to reduce the communication overheads in smart grids and evaluate the approach using real PMU data.

the development of a scalable architecture for the timely processing of smart grid data and its applications.
designing a scalable and efficient data dissemination network that is able to meet the requirements of the smart-grid applications.
developing a systematic methodology for the design of smart-grid applications that can process real-time data efficiently, with low latency and low bandwidth requirements.

our techniques can be used to reduce communication bandwidth and latency for a wide variety of smart grid applications.
